title: "vitest/prefer-expect-type-of"
description: "Require `toBeTypeOf` instead of `expect(typeof value).toBe(...)`"
# Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit below this line.

`expect(typeof value).toBe("string")` only gives `expect` the name of the type. When the test fails, the output compares `"number"` with `"string"` and doesn't show the value. `expect(value).toBeTypeOf("string")` shows it.

The rule reports `typeof` inside `expect` with `toBe` or `toEqual`, with or without `.not`. Despite its name, it asks for the `toBeTypeOf` matcher, not for `expectTypeOf()`.

`--fix` rewrites the assertion. The new text starts with `expect`, also where the file calls that function by another name, as after `import { expect as check }`. `--fix` leaves the fix to `--fix-dangerously` if that `expect` may have no value yet where the code runs: the file assigns to the name, a `var`, `let`, `const` or `import name = ..` line gives the name its value and is neither a `require()` line at the top of the file nor the `const` or `let` line that also declares the name that the code reads now, or the name comes from an `import` in a file that has an `export` of a value. At the top means that nothing but directives, `import` statements, type declarations and other plain `require()` lines stands above it, and that the file has no `export` of a value. Another file could call such an export before the line has run or the `import` has its module.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"vitest/prefer-expect-type-of" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

test("the user has a name", () => {
  expect(typeof user.name).toBe("string");
  expect(typeof user.save).not.toEqual("undefined");
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

test("the user has a name", () => {
  expect(user.name).toBeTypeOf("string");
  expect(user.save).not.toBeTypeOf("undefined");
});
```
